newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish MPs begin debate of Ciller graft charge.
newsitem.headline: Turkish MPs begin debate of Ciller graft charge.

text.p: Turkish deputies on Wednesday began a debate on whether to send Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller to the Supreme Court on a corruption charge relating to her large personal wealth.
After a debate, MPs will vote on whether to impeach Ciller on the third of three charges dealt with this week.

On Tuesday, parliament voted against impeaching Ciller for two corruption charges relating to the sale of state-owned car maker TOFAS and to the electricity company TEDAS during her time as prime minister between 1993 and 1996.
The impeachment of Ciller in any of the three votes would be a serious blow to Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islamist-led government.
The government, in which Ciller also serves as foreign minister, has 278 MPs in the 550-seat assembly. The opposition is around six short of the 276 MPs needed to carry the vote.
Erbakan's coalition faces an opposition censure motion next week which accuses the government of threatening Turkey's secular system with plans to increase the role of Islam in public life.
